# we do a little fork thoughtboi-ing

*blygging about this in order to record my evolution of thoughts*

https://forkcaster.xyz/decent-artlu/0xfb97e388

Farcaster Protocol (Snapchain) is about to hard fork

Merkle sold to Neynar sold to Network State (NS), and NS immediately instituted a digital social contract that many, myself included, consider incompatible with the way we want the future world to work

Cassie has worked mightily (and somewhat inefficiently) to maintain Hypersnap soft-compatibility with Snapchain, but now intends to hard-fork and relay messages between the permissionless portions of both networks

this is likely to be a technical nightmare of distributed systems sync issues, DX seams, and UX footguns. I believe the talent exists (in meatbrains and silicon brains) to eventually solve this, but am not convinced there is a particular reason or good outcome that this will achieve

but anyway. it's happening. such is freedom.

---

A specific technical concern of mine: how to enable user choice of how to view/inspect/validate cryptographically signed messages.

In Lens, you can share links to dozens of protocol clients and the end user maybe kinda eventually just trusts that they know enough about their own client to trust the crypto-brypto-mipto underlying the message transmissions.

Contrast with Mastodon/Threads/ActivityPub, where you trust your federated server owner not to mess with the crypto-brypto-mipto.

And X/Bluesky where you rely on big, fairly centralized but widely distributed entities with fairly open cultures.

And in Blyg, everything is self-owned. So you trust someone not to muck with what they themselves serve up to you. No real crypto signatures.

On Farcaster, it feels like just one really tiny space, so it's easier to think about this problem.

---

# An approach

Problem: some users on Farcaster no longer get shown by the main farcaster client. This is definitionally *censorship*

Solution 1a: any farcaster(dot)xyz cast link can be inspected by changing the domain to forkcaster(dot)xyz or warpcats(dot)com

this route provides to agents a text view of the cast contents, and to humans a rich rendering (including multimedia), plus a redirect mechanism to any FC alt client that offers deeplinks and a full-blown user experience (reactions, feeds, interactive apps, and of course, signer key management)

Solution 1b: an MCP server allows any agent to resolve a canonical link to any alternate link representation

---

# Rejected paths

## endow an entity

A possible solution would be to set up an entity (a DAO, for example) to own a domain (*e.g.*, canonical-farcaster.link) and serve this redirect API and user interface on top of it

the DAO grants credible neutrality and transparency, at the cost of all the capture-resistance tradeoffs that DAOs have to make

I think you lose too many product adopters, at each layer of the DAO onion

## build consensus

Another possible solution is to sit down Balaji, Cassie, and the twenty or so teams building clients, to get a representative of the majority of users to adopt a specific neutral-but-canonical-forever representation

this effort feels like an exercise in herding cats. you might succeed in time, but it won't last. and if it lasts (*e.g.*, United Nations), the scope of possible agreements shrinks over time

## accept niche destiny

Sharing X's links is guaranteed to always work according to their platform rules, and has the benefit of a positive feedback loop of network boosting into things like Trending algos

There's also the fxtwitter service, where a link sharer manually replaces x(dot)com with fxtwitter(dot)com. It enhances link previews, and lets you naturally get back to X by simply clicking. A relative minority of people know about this, and even fewer use it. Some randoms pay for its continued existence--it doesn't really matter as the service is vestigial, not load-bearing

---

Postscript: oops I'm thoughtfarmiiiiinnnnnng ![[5p8r2zmvdbp4abah5q6vvvy4c8 | “Reading Joyce Appleby’s book Relentless Revolution, I’m stru…”]]
